title: An Ancient Ape Fossil in Egypt Could Rewrite Our Family Tree
summary: An ancient ape fossil found in Egypt could rewrite the story of where our ancestors first evolved. The new species, named Masripithecus moghraensis, lived about 17 to 18 million years ago, during the Early Miocene. Its fossilised remains were found at Wadi Moghra in northern Egypt, making it the first definitive fossil ape ever discovered in North Africa. The discovery was described in a study published on March 26, 2026, in the journal Science, by an international team from the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center in Egypt and the University of Southern California. For decades, scientists believed that early apes and their close relatives lived mostly in regions farther south in Africa. Fossil sites in North Africa had turned up ancient monkeys from the same period, but never definitive evidence of apes. That gap helped shape the leading theories about ape evolution. The new fossil may help fill it. "We spent five years searching for this kind of fossil because, when we look closely at the early ape family tree, it becomes clear that something is missing — and North Africa holds that missing piece," said Hesham Sallam, a paleontologist at Mansoura University and senior author of the study. The find is especially important for understanding the origins of crown Hominoidea, the evolutionary group that includes the last common ancestor of all living apes and their descendants. The name combines Masr, the Arabic name for Egypt, with píthēkos, the Greek word for ape. The remains are only lower jaw material, but the jaw is unusually sturdy, with remarkably large canine and premolar teeth. Researchers believe Masripithecus mainly ate fruit, but its teeth were strong enough to handle tougher foods such as nuts or seeds when needed. That flexibility may have helped it survive as the climate changed and food became more seasonal.
why_it_matters: Where our ancestors first lived changes the story of how humans came to be, and one fossil can rewrite it.

keywords.explanation: Fossilised means turned to stone over millions of years.
The Miocene was a period of Earth's history millions of years ago.
Crown Hominoidea is the group of all living apes and their shared ancestors.
Canine teeth are the sharp, pointed teeth near the front of the mouth.
Premolar teeth sit between the canines and the molars and are used for chewing.
Seasonal means changing with the seasons.

background_read: Apes are animals like chimpanzees, gorillas and orangutans, and humans are their close relatives.
A fossil is the preserved remains of a living thing from long ago.
Scientists study fossils to learn how species changed over millions of years.
North Africa is the northern part of Africa, along the Mediterranean Sea.
